makers.name: Dumbwireless
makers.blurb: The shop that proved there was a market.
makers.story: Krigbaum and Stults started Dumbwireless in late 2022 out of a hunch that people wanted less phone and had nowhere to buy it. In March 2023 they sold about $5,000 of phones. By April 2024 that number was roughly $68,000 in a single month. They now carry Light, Punkt and Nokia alongside their own accessories — a Dumbwireless card case sits in Light's own store — and much of their traffic is parents shopping for a first phone.
makers.whyHere: They are the closest thing this space has to a proof of demand, and they are eight miles from this desk.

makers.name: Light
makers.blurb: Ten years of arguing that a phone can just be a phone.
makers.story: Light has spent a decade building a phone designed to be used as little as possible — no browser, no social apps, no store to relapse into. The catalog now runs from a $299 flip to an $899 flagship, and the company sells a $1 zine about going light next to the hardware, which tells you it understands it is selling an argument rather than a device.
makers.whyHere: The anchor tenant of the entire category.

makers.name: Frederik Riedel
makers.blurb: One developer, one breath, a 57% drop.
makers.story: Riedel built one sec in 2021 after a prototype cut his own screen time in half within two weeks. He then did the thing almost nobody in wellness software does: he had it studied. A peer-reviewed collaboration with the Max Planck Institute and Heidelberg University found the app reduced social media use by 57% on average.
makers.whyHere: Evidence, from an independent developer, on a product that costs about ten dollars a year.

makers.name: ClockworkPi
makers.blurb: Modular, open, assembled at your kitchen table.
makers.story: ClockworkPi builds open-source handheld computers as kits — the uConsole being the one that broke containment into the wider cyberdeck scene. Modules are swappable, the community is the documentation, and stock is perpetually a rumor.
makers.whyHere: The Workshop category needs a front door, and this is it.
